Feature composition is not execution

An application-facing DSL should have a small vocabulary and a clear owner for mutable state. Feature selection organizes implementation facilities; it does not define your domain semantics. For example, selecting AST adds construction convenience, but only your application knows whether an add node requires two integers or two vector values. Write those rules before introducing syntax. A wrapper can then reject invalid construction early and preserve enough source information for later diagnostics.

Header-only C++ means definitions are available through inclusion. The D counterpart is a module compiled and linked with the application; it is not a C++ header translated by a preprocessor. Compile DSLtk.d and MetaML.d together with D examples. Avoid importing both modules unqualified when a name such as Session could refer to the generic REPL session or the MetaML session. The examples qualify MetaML.Session to make that distinction explicit.
Concrete callables and ownership

The pipe and predicate wrappers retain callable objects. Capturing a value makes the callable independent of the local variable, while capturing a reference couples its validity to another object's lifetime. A composed object may be returned from a factory, stored in a member or used after its defining scope has exited. Review captures at that ownership boundary, not only at the line containing the lambda.

D generic lambdas can be passed as alias template parameters, for example pipe!((x) => x + x)(). Typed delegates and callable structs can be passed as ordinary values. C++ generic lambdas instead participate through their templated call operators. These are different host mechanisms. Preserve invocation behavior and lifetime first; do not demand identical source spelling. Short-circuit predicate composition also means a later predicate may not run, so side effects should not carry essential work.
AST schemas and side tables

The generic AST stores tags and textual leaves, not a compiler's complete semantic model. Type information, binding identity, comments and source spans need an application strategy. One option is a separate typed AST. Another is a side table keyed by stable node identity, but copied value trees do not supply such identity automatically. Choose that representation before attaching semantic caches to node addresses.

ExprTemplates is a separate facility from ASTNode. ExprTerminal supplies an evaluation protocol, and BinExpr or UnaryExpr stores an expression structure whose eval combines operands. It is suitable for native expression authoring, not automatically a source-located syntax tree. A derived object provides expr_value where required. Inspect terminal ownership carefully: a deferred native expression can outlive the objects it references. Use ASTNode when serialization, inspection and rewriting are primary goals.
Choosing a failure algebra

Maybe expresses expected absence. Result expresses an operation that may fail with a payload. Do not erase a useful error by converting Result to Maybe at a boundary merely because the caller wants a default. First decide whether a missing configuration entry and an invalid entry mean the same thing. Usually the first can use a default while the second must prevent startup.

Result.and_then chains a callback that itself returns Result, whereas map transforms only a successful payload. map_err changes diagnostic representation without touching successful values. Free optional helpers map, flat_map, filter and or_else provide similar convenience around host optional types. Their presence does not make all combinations lawful in the presence of exceptions or side effects. Test that error branches bypass success callbacks, and ensure a cached computation's key includes every semantic input.
Labeling and recovery boundaries

labeled replaces expected-token labels so errors can name language concepts rather than individual characters. Place labels at meaningful boundaries such as an identifier or an assignment, not around the entire parser where every failure becomes the same vague message. The error merge keeps the furthest position and combines expected labels at equal positions. This is useful evidence when explaining why one alternative was selected.

The parser layer is byte-oriented and does not skip whitespace automatically. Compose whitespace recognition explicitly or introduce a lexer that presents normalized tokens to a higher layer. ParserStage and production handlers can connect parsed values to actions, but actions should not publish irreversible state before the enclosing parse succeeds. Separate recognition, construction and publication when you need predictable recovery. Backtracking is a control-flow tool with a cost, not a substitute for factoring common prefixes.
Grammar object lifetimes

C++ PEGRule metadata and parent grammars contain pointers. Keep the referenced grammar objects alive, and avoid holding a rule reference across an append that can reallocate the vector storing local rules. The source comment claims append-stable references, but the inspected implementation stores local rules in std::vector. That implementation detail warrants a conservative lifetime policy. D grammar objects use reference types and have a different identity model.

Derived PEG definitions visit parent rules before local rules. This ordering means adding a child rule does not necessarily override a matching parent rule. PEG channels attach metadata to matches, with ignore channels marking trivia. Actions and ignore handling should be tested together because the implementation constructs match metadata before invoking an installed action. The pattern compiler supports a bounded syntax; inspect CompiledPattern rather than assuming named recursive productions or every standard PEG operator is available.
Three distinct rewrite engines

RewriteSet traverses AST values bottom-up and repeats passes. A matching rule marks the pass changed even if its replacement is structurally equal, so a rule that always matches can consume max_iterations without making progress. The returned tree does not include a stop report. Compare structural equality yourself or use the explicit term reducer when the application must distinguish a normal form from a limit stop.

TermRewriteSystem applies first-order rules in a chosen outermost or innermost strategy. EGraph instead inserts alternatives and merges equivalence classes. These engines share concepts but not operational semantics. Do not present a RewriteSet fixed-point loop as equality saturation. Preserve a written rule contract: required shape, semantic preconditions, allowed effects, integer model and termination measure. Quoting matters because an atom beginning with a question mark can be a variable only when the representation marks it as such.
Graph algorithms and shared reduction

DirectedGraph supports breadth-first and depth-first traversal, topological sorting, strongly connected components and DOT output. A multigraph can contain parallel edges, so algorithms and tests should not silently assume one edge per source-target pair. IDs can become invalid after removal; graph storage uses optional entries rather than recycling every hole into an unrelated node. Keep validity checks at plugin and external-data boundaries.

Term unification differs from matching because variables may occur on both sides. The occurs check prevents binding a variable to a term containing itself. TermGraph reduction redirects incoming edges to a replacement and therefore implements shared reduction. Garbage collection takes explicit roots and removes unreachable nodes. Reconstructing a shared graph as a tree can duplicate work or storage, so use to_term for inspection deliberately rather than in every hot-path operation.
Rebuild and extraction invariants

After e-class unions, parent expressions that previously had different child IDs can become congruent. rebuild canonicalizes child representatives, hash-conses again and merges newly equal parents until stable. This is essential bookkeeping, not an optional cleanup pass. Public queries that call rebuild may therefore do nontrivial work even when their names sound like simple lookups.

Rules must not invent unbound right-hand variables, and concrete additions cannot contain unbound patterns. Saturation callbacks receive rule and match information that can support tracing. Keep tracing bounded because it may generate much more data than the extracted expression. The extractor relaxes node-count costs until stable and requires a finite representative. A target-aware extension would need a documented cost model and legality checks; the current node-count heuristic is a useful baseline rather than a universal optimality claim.
Protocol selection and chart parsing

BinaryStream.next recognizes a regex token at the current cursor. It rejects an empty token because a token consumer must advance. Raw reads return views, whereas write may change backing storage. Document those lifetimes in a binary-format wrapper. Serializer and Deserializer are protocols around a user backend's encode and decode operations; they do not choose JSON, CBOR or an on-disk schema for the application.

CFG terminals are lexer-produced token strings. Earley chart items track production, dot and origin, with an attached first-discovered tree. The implementation deduplicates these item coordinates, so it does not retain every ambiguous derivation. Use grammar validation before accepting plugin rules. For a deterministic programming language, specify operator precedence and associativity through productions rather than relying on whichever derivation happens to be discovered first.
Includes, scripts and source fidelity

Preprocessor exposes include and script callbacks. The host decides which filenames are readable and whether a script language bridge exists at all. The script hook does not bundle a Lua runtime. Set expansion and include-depth limits, and translate missing includes into user diagnostics. If preprocessing changes offsets, a direct span into expanded text cannot automatically identify the original source location.

DiagnosticBag groups diagnostics and filtering, while render_diagnostic presents source excerpts and labels. A fix object describes an edit, but applying it safely still requires version checking against the user's current text. Preserve half-open ranges internally and translate to editor coordinates only at the UI boundary. Unicode display width and CRLF normalization should have explicit tests. Structured codes and spans are generally more stable regression fixtures than complete terminal output.
Protocols, reflection and task policy

Enum reflection has a large compatibility surface: names, values, casts, flags, iteration and enum-indexed containers. C++ aliases expose the bundled magic_enum implementation, including compiler-dependent range discovery. D uses declared members and offers EnumArray, EnumBitset and EnumSet. Duplicate numeric values have naming consequences. A public text format should define whether aliases are accepted and what canonical name is emitted.

TaskPipeline composes named Task operations and records state. TaskPolicy describes sequencing behavior in the supplied task runner; do not infer a general thread pool or asynchronous scheduler from the word pipeline. AbstractIO defines read, write and eof protocol expectations, and write_all must handle partial progress. A backend returning zero without a clear end condition can violate the caller's assumptions. Protocol adapters need failure and short-write fixtures, not just a successful in-memory demonstration.
Evaluation units and commit points

run_program iterates Checker::units, checks a unit in a child scope, commits that scope and then executes. This ordering explains why a script is not an all-or-nothing database transaction. Earlier units and host effects can survive later failure. For reloadable configuration, prepare a separate candidate session and publish it only after validation rather than attempting to reverse arbitrary execution.

RunMode distinguishes evaluation and presentation behavior. eval returns the last value or Unit, while run_source and run_file return RunReport with errors, warnings and output text. declare is intended for host-supplied source and suppresses checker chatter through a temporary quiet setting. A host should choose the API matching its reporting needs instead of calling eval and then trying to reconstruct discarded warning information from a formatted transcript.
The runtime value boundary

Value has a kind tag plus scalar fields or an owned object. Strings, lists, aggregates, closures, constructors, modules and foreign objects have different representation classes. Use helpers such as str_of, list_to_vec and agg_of only after establishing the appropriate kind. A handwritten cast that guesses representation can turn a language error into native undefined behavior.

Core integer helpers intentionally implement a wrapping model, while Int.checked_add, checked_sub and checked_mul return Option for checked operations. Floating values need special handling for NaN, infinities and negative zero. String length and substring primitives use byte positions. Host::Conv supplies a documented set of conversions, not arbitrary C++ reflection. Treat Value pass-through as a low-level escape hatch requiring a clear ownership and type contract.
Recursion, sections and tacit authoring

Named recursive definitions use the parser's rec-aware binding forms. Keep recursion tests small enough to distinguish a type problem from depth exhaustion. The interpreter tracks both call and evaluation depth. Tail-position structure can influence behavior, but users should not assume every source-level tail recursion becomes a constant-stack native loop without inspecting the evaluator path.

MetaML also recognizes tacit parameters such as $1 and section holes such as #1 inside parentheses. Holes are numbered from one and are rejected outside a section context. Composition and concatenative forms have their own parser precedence and runtime stack behavior. These facilities can make a domain vocabulary compact, but an API guide should first demonstrate an equivalent explicit lambda so readers understand the argument flow before adopting terse authoring syntax.
Inference mechanics and API types

TypeNode represents variables, constructors, functions, rows and other inferred structure. The unifier records links, performs occurs checks and supports rollback or commit bookkeeping. Generic variables are instantiated at use sites. Numeric constraints prevent an arithmetic function from being mistaken for a completely unconstrained polymorphic identity. TypePrinter is a presentation layer over this graph.

Rows let a selector require one field while retaining an unknown remainder. A closed record construction and an open record parameter are different type situations. Public embedding functions should still enforce units, ranges and resource identities that are not expressed by the inferred type. Type aliases improve readability but do not automatically create distinct runtime representations. When a domain needs an abstract type, use module signatures and the implemented ascription semantics deliberately.
Pattern coverage and guarded alternatives

Patterns include literals, variables, wildcards, constructors, tuples, records and lists. A match first establishes structural compatibility, then evaluates any guard in the extended environment. Guard failure proceeds to a later alternative. Branch types must unify, which prevents a decision function from returning a Boolean in one case and an unrelated string in another.

A warning about non-exhaustive or redundant patterns is not the same as a fatal type error. Inspect RunReport.warnings when building a publication gate and choose which warning codes your application treats as blockers. Do not globally disable warning categories merely to keep a sample quiet. A language Result constructor and a host Result wrapper remain separate even when they use similar names; document both failure layers in every external API.
Signatures, functors and imports

A module signature can include types and values. Transparent ascription preserves type relationships differently from opaque ascription, represented by Asc in the source. Functor syntax accepts a named module parameter with a signature and requires a struct body. It is a module-level abstraction rather than an ordinary function on Value arguments. Test generative type identity with deliberately incompatible clients before promising an abstract module interface.

Imports resolve relative to source location and configured search roots, and the session tracks imported canonical paths. Cyclic or repeated imports need dedicated fixtures. A module path in an expression is different from a filesystem import string. Separate packaging decisions from language namespace decisions: an installation may move on disk without changing the exported module vocabulary if resolution is configured intentionally.
Trust in explicit primitive signatures

The typed bridge derives arity and type from FnTraits and Conv specializations. The explicit overload trusts a supplied MetaML type string and callback, so the host is responsible for consistency between declared type and Value handling. A callback must check low-level kinds before extracting payloads unless the trusted bridge already establishes them. Never let a plugin register a polymorphic type it cannot implement safely.

host::Conv covers integers, floats, Boolean, strings, optional values, lists, pairs and Value. A void native result maps to Unit. Capturing state in a registered function couples session lifetime to that state. Prefer owned shared resources or an enclosing owner that closes the session before destroying captures. A callback returning a language closure or foreign object requires an additional lifetime review beyond the scalar examples in this chapter.
REPL integration and editor state

ReplLanguage adapts MetaML to the generic DSLtk REPL Session policy. It supplies parse, evaluation, type and error formatting operations, while install_directives adds language-specific commands. The generic REPL tracks complete, incomplete and failed parse states. A trailing delimiter can therefore request more input instead of being treated as a final error immediately.

An editor or REPL needs a source-generation policy. Retained programs and source maps grow with successful interactions, and callbacks may keep values alive. For long-running tools, periodically rebuild a clean environment from the approved source set rather than accumulating every exploratory evaluation forever. Keep asynchronous UI diagnostics associated with the source version that produced them. Rendered carets from a previous buffer version should never be applied as fixes to current text.
Threading and containment boundaries

spawn_interp creates a fresh interpreter sharing session resources and snapshots selected lookup and capability state. It restricts loader and module operations and applies additional background restrictions. That does not make arbitrary concurrent access to the foreground session safe. The checker, loader and source maps have their own mutable state. Document which thread owns each API.

Shutdown callbacks must signal every worker before waiting. A wait callback that joins a worker dependent on an unsignaled sibling can deadlock under a naive one-resource-at-a-time teardown. Output sinks run under a mutex and should not recursively call session output. Native capabilities are not a security sandbox: blocking I/O, memory use and native crashes need operating-system isolation if the trust model requires containment of untrusted policies.
Pinning sources and evidence

The vendor directory contains byte-identical copies of the four uploaded sources under canonical filenames so their internal include and import names work. SOURCE-MAP.md records hashes and the original names. This is a source-pinned guide, not a claim about future releases with the same version string. Rerun examples whenever either library changes and investigate changed results before updating a golden fixture.

C++ examples are compiled together for fast validation and remain separate standalone programs. The D examples are source-reviewed but not compiler-validated in this environment. The build tools expose a separate D test target and report a missing compiler as a limitation rather than a pass. texlua builds the book without requiring Python; Python is used only for optional example generation, validation and development reports. The pre-generated LaTeX sources are sufficient for normal builds.
Formula tool acceptance contract

The complete formula program reads one expression, rejects quoted numeric atoms and unknown operators, validates binary arity recursively and evaluates the pure expression using an explicitly defined unsigned arithmetic model. It normalizes with four identity rules and verifies that before and after values agree. Exit zero means normal form, exit two means a rewrite budget stop, and exit one means invalid input or another failure.

This tool deliberately does not advertise a general algebra system. It has no variables, effects, division, arbitrary precision, distributivity or code generation. Those extensions require new semantics and validation. The e-graph lesson shows an alternative optimization architecture with the same identity laws. Compare performance only after giving both engines the same accepted inputs, rules and budget accounting. Source fixtures and negative cases are included with the standalone program.
Policy service publication contract

The complete decision example validates that allow applied to an Int has Bool type and checks both accepted and rejected fixtures. A candidate returning the wrong type or the wrong boundary decision is rejected. The active session is replaced only after all checks pass. A deliberately bad candidate demonstrates that the previous generation continues working after reload failure.

The sample is a synchronous service core, not an HTTP daemon or a concurrent policy server. A production adapter needs request ownership, timeouts, process containment where appropriate and a strategy for retiring old sessions after in-flight work finishes. Avoid embedding request text into source. Either register typed fact callbacks with per-request ownership or call a prepared function through a documented value bridge. Preserve an explicit error outcome instead of turning every interpreter failure into an unexplained denial.
